newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gehe downplays Unichem claims on Lloyds bid.
newsitem.headline: Gehe downplays Unichem claims on Lloyds bid.

text.p: German pharmacutical group Gehe AG said on Monday that an announcement by British drugs wholesaler and retailer Unichem plc that it had acceptances for 10.1 percent of Lloyds Chemists' shares was "purely a formality".

"Unichem already said that that it had around this level of acceptances and this announcement is a pure formality, a question of a few digits behind the decimal point. It shows that acceptances on both sides are still very low," a spokesman for Gehe AG told Reuters.

Unichem and Gehe have both launched bids for the pharmacy chain operator Lloyds, which last month told investors to sit tight in the event that the bidders increase their offers in the long-running and hotly-contested takeover battle.

Unichem said earlier that it held 10.1 percent of Lloyds, including acceptances representaing about 0.4 percent of the target's ordinary shares, barely changed from the level it reported about a month ago.
Gehe said on December 23 that it had received valued acceptances of its offer representing about 0.16 percent of Lloyds' ordinary shares.
Gehe's offer is made up entirely of cash, while Unichem's bid is made up of shares and cash.
Both companies have until January 17 to raise their bids, and the Gehe spokesman said that the company would continue to wait.
Unichem previously held some 12.3 million shares, representing around 9.7 percent of Lloyds.
